SEC F1: appendAudit (services/audit.js) calls currentAppRole(q) after check(entry) and before lockChain, and throws TypeError unless the role is platform. Probe on PGlite (migrated, login role): two appends under withPlatform work and verifyAudit gives ok, count 2; the same append under withTenant and in a transaction with no role set both throw 'audit: the writer runs only under platform settings' and audit_log still has 2 rows. The developer's I1 (a file outside the listed write set) is accepted by decisions/0137 Addition 4.
SEC F2: addressKey in http/rate-limit.js is used for the setup, login and reset keys (not for 'user', whose subject is the session id) and for the admin delay key in routes/auth.js. Probe over 13 inputs: an IPv4 address stays whole; '2001:db8::', '2001:db8::1' and '2001:0db8:0:0:1:2:3:4' all give 2001:db8:0:0::/64; a different 4th group gives a different key; '::', '::1', an IPv4 tail ('64:ff9b::1.2.3.4', '1:2:3:4:5:6:1.2.3.4') and 'unknown' behave as designed. ip_hmac columns of sessions and audit keep the whole address, as the design says.
SEC F3: uat-login opens the file once with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW, refuses ELOOP as a link, checks regular file and mode with fstat on that descriptor, reads from it and closes it in finally; the win32 refusal still comes first, so the missing O_NOFOLLOW on Windows is never reached. Read only: the success path and the swapped-link case need Linux (the developer's I2; the Linux CI job).
SEC F5: password() calls deleteUnusedResets(req.q, row.id) after deleteOtherSessions and before the audit row, in the same request transaction; the statement already existed in auth-store.js.
SEC F4: a named residual row is added to design section 7 (the pool of 3 connections held through scrypt), measured after the deploy; section 19 has one line per fix with its test line for step 5. No code change expected, none made.

findings.what: An IPv6 text that is not a normal client address collapses into a shared bucket: '::', '::1' and a hex-written mapped address such as '::ffff:102:304' all key to 0:0:0:0::/64. On Node the socket gives the dotted mapped form, which client-ip.js already turns into IPv4, and on Vercel the header is a normal address, so no real client is affected.
findings.fix: None needed now. If a hex mapped form is ever seen in a log, make client-ip.js normalise it to IPv4 before addressKey.

findings.what: The open has no O_NONBLOCK: a file swapped for a FIFO between the lstat and the open would block the script on the open. It needs a local attacker with write access to the owner's secret folder and only hangs the script; the fstat check that follows would refuse it.
findings.fix: Optional: add fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK to the open flags.
